content.text:
`saveAll` in `store.js` could resolve before the writes finished. It called `items.forEach(async …)`, and `forEach` ignores the promises its callback returns. So the function returned `items.length` right away. Any write that was still running at that point was unawaited, and a failed write became an unhandled rejection instead of rejecting `saveAll`.

I replaced the loop with `await Promise.all(items.map((item) => db.put(item.id, item)))`. The writes still run concurrently, as before. `saveAll` now resolves only after every write is stored, and it rejects if any write fails, which is what the comment above the function says it does.

I added two tests: one with a slow `put` (the case that exposed the bug) and one checking that a failed write rejects. All 3 tests pass.
